title: Integration Onramp: Seller Sandbox Playbook (Draft)
content:
Purpose:
Provide a compact, replicable playbook sellers can use during technical pilot kickoff to accelerate integration, demonstrate Redwood economics, and validate fallback/resilience plans. This is designed for field sellers + an SRE/SE co-pilot in a 4-week pilot. Draft / iterative; intended to be converted into a short slide deck and a 1-pager.

Audience:
- Technical sellers (SEs) running pilot workshops
- Account executives needing quick talking points
- Solutions engineers enabling integration teams at customer

TL;DR (30s script for seller):
- "We help you make inference predictable: show us one endpoint you care about, we’ll prove throughput, latency, and cost with a guarded pilot. If capacity or quality varies, we’ll run defined fallbacks so your user experience stays online. We measure actual token economics during the pilot so your CFO can sign off after week 2."

High-level pilot goals (4-week cadence):
- Week 0 (pre-kickoff): align objectives, collect schema, get sample traffic
- Week 1: sandbox integration + smoke tests; baseline latency and token mix
- Week 2: synthetic load & canary, measure per-route economics and error modes
- Week 3: soft cutover on a small percentage of users, validate fallback scripts
- Week 4: handoff + proposal for Dedicated/Reserved capacity or Hosted commit

Value props to surface during call:
- Unified API across hosted/dedicated/private — same integration surface for POC -> production
- Cost controls: suggested batching+cache profile shown against your sample traffic (est. savings % by end of week 2)
- Reliability-first routing and automatic fallback to cheaper-compatible variants when needed
- Observability: token-level cost and latency breakdowns you can share with finance

Quick battlecard snippets (one-liners for seller):
- Customer: "What if latency spikes?"
  - Seller: "We route requests by latency SLO and have an automated fallback to a lower-cost variant with identical interface — your app stays responsive while we remediate."

- Customer: "How do we prove cost before committing?"
  - Seller: "Pilot measures your token mix and runs a model-fit analysis; we show projected spend with and without batching/quantization in our console by day 10."

- Customer: "Can you run in our VPC/on-prem?"
  - Seller: "Yes — we have a private deployment option and can supply a minimal on-prem package for pilots requiring air-gapped setups; typical lead time varies by infra but we can do a light-weight VPC pilot in 2 weeks."

Objection handling frames (short):
- "We already have infra": propose a hybrid pilot where a portion of traffic is routed to Redwood for apples-to-apples performance/cost comparison.
- "Security/compliance concerns": surface KMS/HSM and audit log capabilities; offer a non-prod on-prem snapshot + per-request tracing for the pilot.
- "We need predictable latency": suggest routing policy + soft canary immediately; include an SLA-lite agreement for pilot window.

Recommended pilot artifacts to prepare (seller checklist):
- Customer contact list (engineer + platform + procurement)
- Sample request logs (5k–50k requests) and schema file
- A short prioritized route list (1–3 endpoints to measure)
- Expected traffic profile (p50/p95 latency targets, token lengths distribution)
- Test account created in console + temporary API key

SE playbook: smoke test script (to share in SE channel)
- 1) Run schema validation against sample payloads
- 2) Send 100 warmup requests to populate KV cache
- 3) Measure cold vs warm latency on 100 sequential requests
- 4) Run a 2-minute burst at estimated peak QPS and collect p50/p95/p99
- 5) Trigger fallback (simulate model unavailable) and verify response format and error codes

Fallback scripts (operational snippets for sellers to read aloud):
- "If host latency > SLA for > 2m: flip routing to regional variant A while we queue remediation. Notify SE and open incident bridge with template [JIRA-INCIDENT-PILOT]."
- "If top-of-prompt quality regression detected in eval set: immediately reduce production traffic to 10% and roll to pre-verified model variant via console rollout API."

Pilot success metrics (what we report at end of week 2 and week 4):
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 against SLA baseline
- Cost per 1k tokens by route (with and without batching)
- Error rate (HTTP 5xx and timeouts) and recovery time after fallback
- Quality regression delta on curated prompt set (pass/fail + short examples)
- Estimated monthly spend to reach target throughput (hosted vs dedicated)

Slide-by-slide sketch for a 6-slide seller deck (to convert later):
1) Pilot objective & success criteria (what we will measure)
2) Integration plan & timeline (4-week milestones)
3) Quick proof: sample kpi snapshot (mock numbers)
4) Fallback & resilience story (operational scripts + SLAs)
5) Commercial outcomes (estimated savings and commitment options)
6) Ask & next steps (data we need and timeline to kick off)

Operational templates (to paste into Slack/email during kickoff):
- Kickoff request template: "Please share sample logs (S3 link) and a contact who owns traffic shaping. We will provision a sandbox API key within 48 hours."
- Incident bridge template: "Pilot [account] — fallback triggered at [time]. Impact: [routes]. Current action: routing to variant X. SE assigned: [name]."

Open questions for product/engineering (to triage):
- Can we automate a one-click batching suggestion in console based on uploaded sample logs? (JIRA: GTMIN-742)
- What is smallest private-deploy bundle we can ship for air-gapped customer pilots? (constrain: on-prem ops lead time)
- Can console surface a side-by-side spend forecast for hosted vs dedicated for the last 30 days of pilot traffic?

Next steps (owner & timeline):
- Maya Singh: finalize playbook text and convert to a 6-slide deck (due 2026-02-28)
- Alex Chen: implement the smoke-test script as a runnable Python example and add to repo (due 2026-03-07)
- Priya Patel: craft a one-page pilot legal addendum template for pilot SLA-lite (due 2026-03-03)

Notes to self / rough ideas (keep informal here):
- Consider a "pilot sandbox" badge in Console that auto-applies lightweight monitoring + a pre-approved fallback policy
- Potential small experiment: offer a finance-ready PDF showing estimated token economics after 7 days — A/B with/without batching suggestions
- Keep language short for seller one-pager; focus on three things buyers care about: latency, cost, risk.

End of draft.
